      - img "Interactive linear pair construction": A O B C 72° 108°
      - heading "LIVE MEASUREMENTS" [level=3]
      - text: ∠AOC = 72° ∠COB = 108°
      - strong: Sum = 180° (Linear Pair)
      - progressbar
      - text: "Result: ∠AOC and ∠COB form a linear pair and sum is 180°."
    - article:
      - heading "💡 WHY IT WORKS" [level=2]
      - paragraph: A linear pair consists of two adjacent angles whose non-common arms are opposite rays (a straight line).
      - paragraph: They partition a straight angle, so their measures always sum to 180°.
      - img: 68° 112°
      - complementary: 💡 Key idea Adjacent + opposite non-common arms = linear pair ⇒ sum = 180°.
    - article:
      - heading "☆ WORKED EXAMPLE" [level=2]
      - paragraph: If ∠AOC = 72°, then ∠COB = ?
      - img: 72° 108°
      - text: Solution
      - paragraph: By Linear Pair Axiom, ∠AOC + ∠COB = 180° 72° + ∠COB = 180° ∠COB = 108°
      - text: Hence, ∠COB = 108°.
    - article:
      - heading "△ MISCONCEPTION ALERT" [level=2]
      - paragraph: Supplementary angles need not form a linear pair unless they are adjacent and their non-common arms are opposite rays.
      - text: Not a linear pair (not adjacent)
      - img: 130° 50°
      - paragraph: 130° + 50° = 180°, but angles are not adjacent. So they do not form a linear pair.
      - text: ⏱ Remember Adjacency + correct arms are both required.
    - 'heading "◎ CHALLENGE: Prove the outer rays are opposite" [level=2]'
    - complementary:
      - paragraph: Adjust the two adjacent angles so that their sum is 180°. Then verify that the outer rays are opposite.
      - text: ∠AOC target 65°
      - button "∠AOC target 65° + 65": −
      - button "+"
      - slider "∠AOC target": "65"
      - text: ∠COB target 115°
      - button "∠COB target 115° + 115": −
      - button "+"
      - slider "∠COB target": "115"
      - text: Keep O on the line. Use Converse mode to build the line when sum = 180°.
      - button "Switch to Converse mode"
